about.title: Cultural Heritage of Cooperativism
about.what_is_cch_description: Cooperative Cultural Heritage (CCH) refers to the collective legacy of cooperatives that have shaped societies, economies, and cultures across the world. It encompasses both Tangible Elements such as sites, institutions, museums and legacy enterprises, and intangible traditions, including elements of local practice & traditions that safeguard cooperative values, practices, and governance systems passed down through generations. Together, these elements tell the story of how cooperation has contributed to sustainable livelihoods, community resilience, social justice, and cultural identity.
about.ica_programme_desc1: The ICA's ambitious undertaking to establish a Cooperative Cultural Heritage (CCH) inscription program signifies a recognition of the cooperative movement's enduring legacy and its unique contribution to global human history and, through its continuing service, to sustainable development.
about.ica_programme_desc2: This initiative aims to systematically identify, document, and safeguard the tangible and intangible manifestations of cooperative principles across continents.
about.ica_programme_desc3: In 2025, the ICA-CCH programme launched information about twenty-five physical sites that embody the culture of cooperation at the local and national levels.
about.goal1_description: Identifying, through consultations with WG member, and recognizing, through a digital map of the world, 25 geographical sites of undisputed cooperative heritage at the inter/national level.
about.goal2_description: Developing, through consultations with cultural heritage professionals and legal experts, the first version of international standards and exploring potential certification mechanisms concerning Cooperative Cultural Heritage.
about.goal3_description: Launching, a global communications and public-relations campaign to make widely known the contribution and potential of cooperatives to culture and sustainable development.
about.programme_desc1: This programme serves the long-term goal of the ICA to facilitate the collection of information and key insights about those places and practices of cooperation that are not widely known.
about.programme_desc2: The objective is indeed to go back to the first principles of the ICA, which is to make known the co-operators of the world, and their work, globally.
about.preserving_desc1: The Cooperative Cultural Heritage Programme represents a milestone in recognizing and preserving the rich history of cooperation that has shaped communities worldwide.
about.preserving_desc2: Through systematic documentation and international recognition, we ensure that future generations can learn from and be inspired by the cooperative movement's enduring contributions to society.
about.members_description: The Cooperative Cultural Heritage Programme brings together cooperative organizations, cultural institutions, and communities from around the world to preserve and celebrate cooperative heritage.

tangible.description: Physical places, buildings, settlements, and infrastructure that embody the history and legacy of cooperative enterprise. These include cooperative stores, factories, housing complexes, agricultural facilities, and landscapes directly associated with cooperative activity. Tangible CCH represents the material foundations of cooperation, visible in the built environment and cultural landscapes shaped by cooperative governance.

home.principles_title: Principles for Identifying Cooperative Cultural Heritage
home.principles_desc: These principles guide the identification and recognition of cooperative cultural heritage elements.
home.criteria_desc: A thirteen point set of international standards on Cooperative Cultural Heritage was drawn up by the ICA Working Group on CCH in fall 2025. These standards, the first of their kind, will build on experiences through 2026, by which time, the ICA aims to list at least 50 CCH sites and 15 CCH intangible elements (through a separate set of criterions) from across all the regions, representing all ICA sectors, selected through a nomination process, open to the members of the ICA and their constituents. A unique ICA-CCH label will be granted to the selected sites that meet all the 13 criterions along with a Statement of Recognition, in a post launch (November 2025) exercise.

criteria.title: Criteria & Nominations
criteria.subtitle:
ICA Standards of Cooperative Cultural Heritage
based on the Statement on the Cooperative Identity
criteria.assessment_desc: A thirteen-point set of international standards on Cooperative Cultural Heritage was drawn up by the ICA Working Group on CCH in fall 2025. These standards, the first of their kind, will build on experiences through 2026, by which time, the ICA aims to list at least 50 CCH sites and 15 CCH intangible elements (through a separate set of criteria) from across all regions, representing all ICA sectors, selected through a nomination process open to ICA members and their constituents. A unique ICA-CCH label will be granted to selected sites that meet all 13 criteria, along with a Statement of Recognition, in a post-launch (November 2025) exercise.
criteria.description: The International Cooperative Alliance (ICA) invites its member organizations to take an active role in identifying, celebrating, and safeguarding the living legacy of cooperation around the world. The process of recognizing Cooperative Cultural Heritage Sites is not only an act of preservation but also a reaffirmation of the cooperative identity—rooted in values of democracy, solidarity, and collective progress. This initiative seeks to shine a light on the spaces, institutions, and communities that embody the cooperative spirit across generations. From historic buildings and archives to contemporary centers of learning and community action, these sites serve as tangible witnesses to the cooperative movement's profound contribution to social and cultural development. They are places where the cooperative ethos has shaped livelihoods, fostered innovation, and strengthened communities through shared ownership and mutual aid. Through a transparent and participatory nomination process, ICA member organizations are encouraged to identify and propose sites in their countries that meet the established criteria. These criteria ensure that recognized sites not only possess historical and cultural significance but also continue to nurture cooperative education, engagement, and sustainability in the present day. The nomination process provides an opportunity for members to document, interpret, and share their cooperative heritage with both local and global audiences. Ultimately, this Charter and its recognition framework aim to weave cooperative heritage into the broader fabric of world culture making it visible, accessible, and celebrated as part of humanity's shared story. Each nominated site becomes a living testament to cooperation as a force for social good, reminding us that the cooperative model is not only an economic structure but also a cultural tradition that connects past, present, and future generations.
criteria.charter_title: Charter of the Cooperative Cultural Heritage
criteria.preamble_desc: Recognizing that cooperatives are not only enterprises but also bearers of culture, history, and identity, this Charter establishes a framework for the recognition and safeguarding of cooperative cultural heritage sites. These criteria aim to ensure that cooperative heritage is preserved, celebrated, and integrated into wider cultural narratives while continuing to inspire present and future generations in line with the values of democracy, equity, solidarity, and sustainability. This Charter affirms the commitment of the cooperative movement to recognize, preserve, and promote its cultural heritage. By adopting these criteria, cooperative heritage sites shall become living symbols of solidarity, education, and international cooperation.
criteria.nomination_desc: Access the form to nominate elements of Cooperative Cultural Heritage from your country. Please feel free to contact
criteria.nomination_contact: if you need any assistance or support.

events.title:
Cooperative Cultural
Heritage Events
events.description: This page highlights events organized by the International Cooperative Alliance (ICA) and its member organizations dedicated to celebrating, exploring, and safeguarding cooperative cultural heritage. From conferences and exhibitions to workshops, anniversaries, and local heritage celebrations, these events bring together cooperators, researchers, and communities to share experiences and deepen understanding of the cooperative identity as a living cultural legacy.
events.submit_description: If your organization is hosting an event related to cooperative heritage — past, present, or future — you are invited to submit the details to be featured here. Sharing your event helps strengthen our global network and ensures that cooperative culture continues to inspire across borders.
